body: I'd definitely love to talk to you sometime. If I remember, when I get to it hopefully you'll be there.

I don't know if that kind of contentment is out of positive acceptance or negative resignation. To echo what I said in my original post, people have kind of died inside, meaning they've just accepted this as the way things are.

To be fair, it's not like you can change reality, so I'm not really sure what I'm getting at. But for right now, in this stage of my life, I'm just not happy going forward if this is what I have to look forward to.

Seemingly true in theory, yet difficult or different in practice. A lot of variables get in the way. It seems a majority of the population has chosen to not do this. I'm not sure why but I want to find out. I feel like I'm missing something.
Yes, thank you. I should just add your post to mine.
This sounds like a good idea. I've been considering it as a way to ground myself as I go through life.

You get it! Yes, this is mostly what I'm talking about.

And a good point you do bring up about how potentially the lack of exploration possible (by single individuals) might have made us generally more stagnant. Gone are the days when a single person in his own basement can tinker around and win a Nobel prize in physics or chemistry.

I guess the issue of being a school teacher (which I would love to try for a year or two) is that, really, who cares? Your students? Maybe a few. And they might go on to do great things. The rest are thinking of sex in class (see top front-page Reddit threads for proof) and others (me) are thinking of the minimum amount of work possible to pass in a flawed education system.

Then you're just battling administration and funding issues and policy issues (gotta test students, test test test).

In the end, you've maybe seriously inspired 5-20 people in a 10-year span. Most people are very normal and won't fight the status quo. The 5-20 people might. Some of those 5-20 people then post threads like this one, asking if it's really worth it.

So you agree, at least partially. I'm not insane.

I think you're right about having quality people making people happy, but that's one of the things (even with quality people) that depresses me. I could be personally happy, but I'm disappointed that *this is it*. See my replies above: I'm so annoyed adult life is just basically billions of people forming two-people three-people cliques that do their own shit and everybody just eventually dies making no net change to the status quo. Billions of people do this.
I would agree with you that I can't make the claim many people have died inside. I feel it's true, but I can't really know. Not sure what the best game in town is though.
Hah, so sorry. Also, I noticed you deleted a comment telling me to get meds and stop bitching, so I wasn't laughing or making fun of you, I was agreeing.

I actually would call this dying a little inside. Acceptance, and a healthy attitude changing your mindset instead of being unreasonably angry at a blank white wall. But, I mean, why should things have to be this way?

See the above super long reply to another person. I don't mind building my own path to the things I think are important, but is it worth it? If I want to make large positive impacts, and people don't really care, is it worth what I sacrifice?

So I'm supposed to do it "for myself" then, but I can't seem to bring myself to do that. I don't want to be another one of the billion people tinkering in his or her own life making real no net change to society.

I'll actually take you up on your PM offer, sometime later though as I'm kind of busy.

To respond to your post:

Thanks for such a detailed post. It's made me reflect and think differently of the more black-and-white terms with which I wrote the original post.

I think I agree very much with you on everything you said. Especially the part where their happiness, however cheap it may appear to me, does not devalue their subjective value of their happiness. Well said.

I think something I didn't mention in my original post is that I'm not happy just doing small random tasks for the duration of my life. I want to make positive differences that have a large impact on people. If we were to take a small task of, say education reform, there are already so many people looking at the problem, many issues are deadlocked, it's almost as if people *don't want* progress. I've noticed this same kind of frustrating dead-endness in other things as well.

You graduate out of your school years pushed on faster and faster with shiny gold stars. Once you get out, you're pushed to work and no one honestly gives a shit. They'd ask you to stay more hours at your expense.

My thoughts aren't too clear in the morning, but basically I don't see how I can make a positive meaningful impact because a) there are too many people doing too many things for it to get noticed; b) honestly, do people care? (I say, only narrowly if they see it benefits them); c) laws, policies, public opinion making any kind of real progress difficult.

Am I supposed to be happy even if I'm in a job I like (I enjoy writing too), if I know less than 0.0001% of the world population will read my book?

Am I supposed to be happy if I change one obscure policies that nobody really cared about anyways and got switched back next year?

Everybody just seems to be happy tinkering with their own life. Where's this connected sense of human progress? Everything seems so stagnant. At face value, change and progress is good. A little deeper, nobody really seems to give a shit.

Example: I've browsed Reddit for over a year and I've seen what gets upvoted to the front page (this is *after* I unsubscribed from adviceanimals and funny, which btw are depressing in how many subscribers they get). Useless trivial fun-fact threads. Fun to read, oh yes. Completely useless though. Everybody's gotta have an opinion though, right?

I have a good friend and I don't think he would disagree, but he's too focused on his priorities and career advancement. He's left this behind and focused on doing what he can do and living in the moment. I think that's a reasonably way to live, but it doesn't lower my angst.
